newsitem.title: USA: InterSystems sees good trends continuing.
newsitem.headline: InterSystems sees good trends continuing.

text.p: InterSystems Inc said Monday that it expects trends to continue at all its operating divisions and anticipates earnings growth that should accelerate during the rest of 1997 and beyond.
InterSystems reported second quarter earnings from continuing operations of $0.05 a share, compared to a loss of $0.01 a share, the year before.

The company said that sales at its Nebraska division have seen major increases during the period as a result of the continuing strength of the grain industry, which has been investing heavily in capital improvements.
Intersystems said its backlog of more than $6 million is the highest in the company's history going into the third quarter and appears headed higher.
At its Chemtrusion facilities, its fourth production line has been delivered and will be on line in September to meet increased demand.
Customer commitments to fill that line will substantially boost revenues going forward, the company said.
Chemtrusion's Indiana division's first six months of operations performed way beyond expectations, InterSystem said.
It said it has additional manufacturing equipment on order, which will significantly increase next year's capacity.
